recap:
## Decisions
- Keep a back-up plan: a really good, comfortable TV-only remote, since the remote has to be cheap to make [00:16:01]
- Include a lock function so buttons can't be pressed by accident (also safer for kids) [00:17:52]
- ID and UI will work together because their responsibilities overlap [00:19:28]

## Action items
- UI: Work out which buttons the remote needs [00:18:49]
- ID: Work out the casing and what goes inside it [00:18:58]
- ME: Research what users want in a remote, including which buttons are used most often [00:19:36]
- owner not assigned: Research whether the proposed ideas are feasible within the €12.50 production cost [00:12:59]

## Unresolved
- Scope: control the TV plus connected devices like DVD players, or focus on a TV-only remote [00:16:01]
- Form factor: thin remotes that slide out, a two-sided simple/advanced remote, or a flip design with basic buttons outside. UI doubted a two-sided remote would be easy to handle [00:14:37]
- An LCD display with pages for each device was suggested but may be too expensive [00:12:34]
- Selling point: what will make people want to buy it. Options raised were a niche (disabled or visually impaired users) or a very cool look [00:16:34]
- Size: ME suggested medium, but no one else responded [00:11:46]
- Actual component costs are unknown [00:12:53]
